ctDiscreteParsPlot

Source: R/ctDiscretePars.R
ctDiscreteParsPlot.Rd

Plots the output from ctDiscretePars, for model implied regression strengths at specified times for continuous time models fit with ctStanFit. ctStanDiscreteParsPlot is maintained as a backward-compatible alias.

Usage

ctDiscreteParsPlot(
  x,
  indices = "all",
  quantiles = c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975),
  latentNames = "auto",
  ylab = "Coefficient",
  xlab = "Time interval",
  ylim = NA,
  facets = NA,
  splitSubjects = TRUE,
  colour = "Effect",
  title = "auto",
  polygonalpha = 0.1,
  ggcode = FALSE,
  line = c("estimate", "median")
)

Arguments

x

list object returned from ctDiscretePars.

indices

Either a string specifying type of plot to create, or an n by 2 matrix specifying which indices of the output matrix to plot. 'AR' specifies all diagonals, for discrete time autoregression parameters. 'CR' specifies all off-diagonals,for discrete time cross regression parameters. 'all' plots all AR and CR effects at once.

quantiles

numeric vector of length 3, with values between 0 and 1, specifying which quantiles to plot. The default plots 95% credible intervals as the band, and the posterior median at 50% as the line where line does not draw the estimate.

latentNames

Vector of character strings denoting names for the latent variables. 'auto' just uses eta1 eta2 etc.

ylab

y label.

xlab

x label.

ylim

Two values, the lower and upper limits of the y axis. Intervals that extend past them are cut at the edge.

facets

May be 'Subject' or 'Effect'.

splitSubjects

if TRUE, subjects are plotted separately, if FALSE they are combined.

colour

Character string denoting how colour varies. 'Effect' or 'Subject'.

title

Character string. 'auto' generates automatically, NULL can be used to disable title.

polygonalpha

Numeric between 0 and 1 to multiply the alpha of the fill.

ggcode

if TRUE, returns a list containing the data.table to plot (for each curve and time interval, the outer quantiles of the draws as ymin and ymax, and the line as value), and a character string that can be evaluated (with the necessary arguments such as ylab etc filled in). For modifying plots.

line

What the line shows. 'estimate' (the default) draws the effects at the fit's estimate when x carries them (attr(x, 'estimate'), for an optimised fit), and otherwise the middle of quantiles. 'median' draws the middle of quantiles. The band shows the quantiles of the draws.

Value

A ggplot2 object. This can be modified by the various ggplot2 functions, or displayed using print(x).

Details

For a model whose dynamics depend on the state, the curves are computed at one point in the state space, and the subtitle names the point. The default, the population initial state with time dependent predictors at zero, can be far from the data. Choose the point, and whether to linearise or simulate, with ctDiscretePars(state = , method = ).

Examples

data.table::setDTthreads(1) #ignore this line
x <- ctDiscretePars(ctstantestfit)
ctDiscreteParsPlot(x, indices='CR')

#to modify plot:
g <- ctDiscreteParsPlot(x, indices='CR') +
 ggplot2::labs(title='My ggplot modification')
print(g)
